results.evidence: results/formal/case_rank1_ring/metrics.json: APDG mean_iterations=867.26, GDAM (Globally Dual) mean_iterations=500.6, LDAM (Locally Dual) mean_iterations=275.96. results.note: Method names in output file are APDG, GDAM, and LDAM — corresponding to APDG, Globally Dual, and Locally Dual respectively.

results.description: In terms of total computational time in Table 1, APDG is the fastest, followed by Locally Dual, and Globally Dual is the slowest.
results.evidence: File: results/formal/case_rank1_ring/metrics.json (experiment_id=case_rank1_ring, paper_case="Paper case 1: 5 nodes, dimension 40, rank(B)=1, ring graph"). Actual mean_time_seconds: APDG=0.079239s, GDAM (Globally Dual)=0.021262s, LDAM (Locally Dual)=0.010081s. The claim requires APDG < Locally Dual < Globally Dual in time (APDG fastest, Globally Dual slowest). The actual ordering is the exact reverse: LDAM (0.010) < GDAM (0.021) < APDG (0.079). APDG is the slowest, not fastest, and Globally Dual is in the middle, not slowest. Both pairwise constraints fail: APDG (0.079) is NOT faster than Locally Dual (0.010), and Locally Dual (0.010) is NOT faster than Globally Dual (0.021).
results.note: GDAM maps to Globally Dual and LDAM maps to Locally Dual based on naming conventions. The experiment matches ring graph, 5 nodes, rank 1, dim 40 as specified.

results.description: One iteration of either Dual method (Globally Dual or Locally Dual) is more time-consuming than one iteration of APDG.
results.evidence: File: results/formal/case_rank1_ring/metrics.json. Computed time_per_iteration = mean_time_seconds / mean_iterations: APDG = 0.079239s / 867.26 = 9.14e-5 s/iter; GDAM (Globally Dual) = 0.021262s / 500.60 = 4.25e-5 s/iter; LDAM (Locally Dual) = 0.010081s / 275.96 = 3.65e-5 s/iter. The claim requires APDG > Globally Dual and APDG > Locally Dual in the sense that APDG is better (lower time per iteration), but the measured data shows APDG has the HIGHEST time per iteration — it is ~2.15x slower per iteration than GDAM and ~2.5x slower than LDAM. Both dual methods are faster per iteration than APDG, directly contradicting the claim.
results.note: The method names in the output file use 'GDAM' and 'LDAM' (not 'Globally Dual'/'Locally Dual'), which appear to correspond to the paper's 'Globally Dual AM' and 'Locally Dual AM' methods. No explicit time_per_iteration field exists; it was computed from mean_time_seconds / mean_iterations.

results.description: All algorithms converge linearly for the first experiment (ring network, 5 nodes, dim(x)=40, rank B=1).
results.evidence:
File: results/formal/case_rank1_ring/history.json (representative seed=42, ring graph, 5 nodes, dim=40, rank B=1). Per-iteration constraint_norm histories are present for all three algorithms. Log-space linear regression over the second half of each trajectory:
- APDG: 939 iters, converged=True, log-slope=-0.00779, R²=0.99939
- GDAM: 496 iters, converged=True, log-slope=-0.01943, R²=0.96918
- LDAM: 277 iters, converged=True, log-slope=-0.03718, R²=0.99488
All slopes are negative and R²>0.96, demonstrating geometric (linear) decay in the error norm. Contraction ratios in the final 20 iterations are approximately constant (mean ~0.962–0.992 with very small std), confirming linear convergence for all algorithms. Config confirmed via resolved_config.json: graph=ring, nodes=5, dimension=40, constraint_rank=1.
results.note: Only the representative run (seed=42) has per-iteration history stored; the metrics.json shows 100 repeats all converged. The claim is about the convergence plot (Figure 1), which corresponds to the representative trajectory, and all three algorithms show clear linear convergence there.

results.description: APDG seems to converge much faster by constraints violation norm at first iterations than the other methods.
results.evidence: results/formal/case_er_rank1_highdim/history.json (experiment: erdos_renyi, 10 nodes, rank=1, methods APDG/GDAM/LDAM matching 'Globally Dual'/'Locally Dual'): At iteration 1, APDG constraint_norm=1029.50 vs GDAM=59776.13 and LDAM=59427.01. APDG remains lower than both GDAM and LDAM for all first 20+ iterations (True in every row of APDG<GDAM and APDG<LDAM comparisons). At iteration 16, APDG reaches ~912.32 while GDAM is ~17459.44 and LDAM ~16885.81 — a ~18x gap. The required ordering APDG > Globally Dual (GDAM) and APDG > Locally Dual (LDAM) under lower_is_better holds throughout the early iterations, confirming the claim that APDG converges much faster by constraints violation norm at first iterations.
results.note: GDAM maps to 'Globally Dual' and LDAM to 'Locally Dual' based on the config file and naming conventions. The config explicitly references 'Paper case 3: 10 nodes, dimension 100, rank(B)=1, Erdos-Renyi p=0.3' and 'Section 7, Figure 3', matching experiment exp3_erdosrenyi_10nodes_rank1.
